entities.summary: Finnian of Movilla was a Christian missionary of Irish origin who played a pivotal role in the spread of Christianity throughout the Roman Empire and beyond. Born in the early 6th century CE, Finnian was educated in the monastic schools of Ireland and later traveled to France and Italy, where he evangelized to the local populations. His missionary work was marked by a series of conversions, including that of King Clotaire I of the Franks, which had far-reaching implications for the development of Christianity in Western Europe. Finnian's legacy can be seen in the numerous monastic foundations he established throughout Gaul and the Iberian Peninsula, which served as centers of learning and spiritual growth. His feast day, celebrated on September 10, is a testament to his enduring impact on the Christian faith. The exact dates of Finnian's birth and death are unknown, but his significance in the annals of Christian history is undeniable.
